items.heading: Write Fewer Skills and Make
items.text: Write Fewer Skills and Make Write Fewer Skills and Make Write fewer skills and make each one checkable. A fresher has no job history, so the skills section is where your proof lives. It should answer one question for the person reading: "Can this person do the three things my job post asks for?".

columns: What it means on your resume
rows: A recruiter scans first and a hiring manager checks later. The skills line must make sense to both: exact tool names for the recruiter, proof for the manager.
Read the job post and find the three tasks it repeats. Your top skills should answer those three tasks, in the same words where true.
One receipt line per core skill, plus one link to the work itself. A link beats a claim every time.
A headline that names the role you want, such as "Entry-level data analyst". A resume that asks for nothing gets nothing.
